Questions

Bucks Balm FAQ

Will tallow balm make my face greasy?
Not when you use the right amount. Bucks Balm is concentrated, so a pea-sized amount covers your whole face. The botanical oils help it absorb, and most of it sinks in within a couple of minutes.
Does it smell like beef?
No. The tallow is slow-rendered and the balm is scented with patchouli, cedarwood and spruce essential oils. It smells like a walk in the woods.
Which size should I buy?
The 1 oz fits a pocket or gym bag. The 2 oz is a good first daily tin. The 4 oz is the best value per ounce and lasts most people several months.
Is it OK for sensitive skin?
It has no synthetic fragrance, and the essential oils are at cosmetic-safe levels. If your skin is sensitive, patch test on your inner arm first.
How long does a tin last?
12–18 months unopened and 6–12 months after opening. Store it somewhere cool and dry. It may soften in heat without affecting quality.

Why Tallow · Why Bucks

Your Skin Already Knows This Fat

Tallow is one of the oldest moisturizers there is. Here's why it works, and why we didn't stop at tallow.

Part 1 · Why TallowPart 2 · Why Bucks
The short answerTallow works on skin because its fats closely match sebum, the oil your skin makes on its own. It's built mostly from oleic, palmitic and stearic acids in similar ratios, and grass-fed tallow carries fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K. That lets it moisturize and support the skin barrier instead of only coating the surface.
~1:1

A close match to sebum

Oleic, palmitic and stearic acids dominate both tallow and your skin's own oil.

26%

Palmitic acid

A main structural fat in skin cell membranes, tied to firmness and barrier strength.

21%

Stearic acid

Helps restore a skin barrier worn down by over-washing or harsh soap.

Grass-Fed Matters

Vitamins in Their Natural Form

Pasture-raised cattle make fat with more CLA, omega-3s and fat-soluble vitamins. They arrive in tallow naturally, not added back in.

A

Supports cell turnover. Also found in our rosehip oil.

D

Plays a role in the skin's own defenses.

E

Antioxidant protection. Also in argan oil and added on its own.

K2

Associated with skin elasticity.

A Short History

Why Tallow Disappeared, and Why It's Back

Thousands of years

Rendered animal fat protects skin across nearly every culture.

Early 1900s

Tallow is a common base for soaps and balms.

Mid-century

Cheaper petroleum and synthetic ingredients take over at scale.

Today

People reading labels go back to ingredients their skin recognizes.

Questions

Tallow Skincare FAQ

Is tallow good for your face?
For most normal to dry skin, yes. Tallow's fats resemble your skin's own oil, so it tends to absorb rather than sit on top. If you're very oily or acne-prone, patch test first.
Does tallow clog pores?
Tallow is generally considered low on the pore-clogging scale because its profile is so close to sebum. Everyone's skin is different, so start small.
Why grass-fed tallow?
Grass-fed, grass-finished cattle produce fat with more CLA, omega-3s and fat-soluble vitamins than grain-fed cattle.
What makes Bucks Balm different from other tallow balms?
Two things: it's dense instead of whipped, and it adds five botanical oils plus beeswax, vitamin E and three essential oils. Most tallow balms stop at tallow and one or two extras.

Is Tallow Good for Your Skin? What the Research Says

By the Buck's Tallow family·8 min read·Updated Oct 2026
In this articleWhy tallow worksGrass-fed vs grain-fedTallow vs lotionWho should skip itFAQSources
Quick answer AEO direct answer · product-neutralYes, for most people with normal to dry skin. Tallow's fatty acids closely resemble sebum, the oil your skin makes, so it tends to absorb and support the skin barrier instead of sitting on top. Grass-fed tallow also carries vitamins A, D, E and K. Very oily or acne-prone skin should patch test first.

Tallow sounds like something from a pioneer cookbook. It is. It's also one of the most skin-compatible moisturizers you can buy, which is why it's back.

Why does tallow work on skin?

Your skin coats itself in sebum, a mix of fats that keeps moisture in. Tallow is built from the same main fatty acids, oleic, palmitic and stearic, in similar proportions. That close match is why it tends to absorb instead of leaving a film.

Petroleum-based moisturizers work differently. They form a seal over the skin, which holds water in but adds nothing to the barrier itself.

That's why the fats in a moisturizer matter more than the word "hydrating" on the label.Bridge sentence

Does grass-fed tallow matter?

Yes. Cattle raised on pasture produce fat with more CLA, omega-3s and fat-soluble vitamins than grain-fed cattle. Those nutrients are part of what makes tallow useful for skin.

Is tallow better than lotion?

It depends on what you need. For dry, rough or wind-chapped skin, tallow usually does more per application.

Tallow balmTypical lotion
Main ingredientAnimal fatWater

If you want to try one, look for a dense, water-free tallow balm with botanical oils rather than a whipped one.Inline link

Who should skip tallow?

If your skin is very oily or prone to severe breakouts, patch test before using tallow on your face. Anyone with a known sensitivity to an essential oil should check the label.

FAQ Feeds FAQ schema

Is tallow good for acne-prone skin?
Some people with mild breakouts do fine with it, but results vary. Patch test on your jawline for a week before using it on your whole face.
How often should I use tallow balm?
Once or twice a day works for most people, usually after a shower and before bed.
Does tallow balm expire?
A water-free balm keeps well. Expect 12–18 months unopened and 6–12 months after opening.

Our Story

Welcome to the Family

Hand crafted and family owned in Minnesota.

Bucks Balm began long before it ever had a label. The name Buck has lived in our family for generations, passed down from my grandfather to my father. The nickname is something I inherited and now get to pass along to my sons. To us it has represented consistency, craftsmanship, and the belief that what you do and what you make should be of high quality and benefit family, friends, and community.

When we set out to create our tallow balm, we didn't rush it. We didn't want to jump on the tallow bandwagon. Instead, we spent years researching, refining, and testing until the formula matched the standard our family has always lived by: if we wouldn't use it ourselves, we won't put it into the world. Every ingredient and its ratio was chosen with intention.

Every member of our family is a part of Bucks Tallow, from product research and development to branding to customer fulfillment and service. It's our way of making sure we deliver on our commitments and standards.

Today, we're proud to share Bucks Balm with the world. Made in Minnesota with grass-fed, grass-finished tallow, restorative oils, and clean, functional ingredients and fragrances, it's created for those who want skincare grounded in research, testing and science.

Welcome to the family.
